Problem Set 3: Electrostatics

Problem 3.1: Coulomb’s Law with Multiple Charges

Three point charges are arranged in a straight line along the x-axis: a charge of +2.0 μC at x = 0 m, a charge of -4.0 μC at x = 3.0 m, and a charge of +3.0 μC at x = 6.0 m. a) Calculate the net electric force on the charge at x = 0 m. b) If a fourth charge of -1.5 μC is placed at x = -2.0 m, calculate the new net force on the charge at x = 0 m.

Problem 3.2: Electric Field Calculations

a) A uniformly charged ring with radius 15 cm has a total charge of +8.0 μC. Calculate the electric field strength at a point 20 cm away from the center of the ring along its axis. b) A non-conducting sphere with radius 5.0 cm has a uniform charge density and a total charge of +2.0 nC. Calculate the electric field at a point 3.0 cm from the center of the sphere.

Problem 3.3: Electric Potential and Potential Difference

A uniform electric field of 4000 V/m is directed along the positive x-axis. a) Calculate the potential difference between points A(x = 0 m, y = 0 m) and B(x = 0.25 m, y = 0.30 m). b) What is the potential difference between points C(x = 0.50 m, y = 0.50 m) and D(x = 0.75 m, y = 0.25 m)? c) How much work would be required to move a charge of +3.0 μC from point A to point C?

Problem 3.4: Electric Potential Energy Calculations

Four point charges are placed at the corners of a square with side length 10 cm: +2.0 μC at (0,0), -3.0 μC at (10 cm,0), +1.0 μC at (10 cm,10 cm), and -2.0 μC at (0,10 cm). a) Calculate the electric potential energy of this system of charges. b) How much work would be required to move the charge at (0,0) to the position (5 cm, 5 cm)?

Problem 3.5: Capacitance Calculations

a) A parallel-plate capacitor has plates of area 0.015 m² separated by 0.50 mm. Calculate its capacitance if the space between the plates is: i. Vacuum ii. Filled with a dielectric material with dielectric constant κ = 3.5 b) If this capacitor is connected to a 12 V battery, calculate: i. The charge stored on each plate ii. The electric field between the plates

Problem 3.6: Gauss’s Law Application

A long, straight wire with uniform linear charge density λ = 4.0 × 10⁻⁹ C/m extends along the z-axis. a) Use Gauss’s law to derive an expression for the electric field at a distance r from the wire. b) Calculate the electric field strength at a distance of 5.0 cm from the wire.

Problem 3.7: Multiple Capacitors

Three capacitors with capacitances of 4.0 μF, 6.0 μF, and 12.0 μF are connected in: a) Series - calculate the equivalent capacitance. b) Parallel - calculate the equivalent capacitance. c) If the series combination is connected to a 9.0 V battery, what is the potential difference across each individual capacitor?

Problem 3.8: Energy Stored in Capacitors

A 2200 μF capacitor is charged to a potential difference of 12 V. a) Calculate the energy stored in this capacitor. b) If this energy were converted to mechanical energy, to what height could it lift a 10 g object? c) If this capacitor is connected in parallel with an uncharged 4700 μF capacitor, what is the final potential difference across each capacitor?

Problem 3.9: Electrostatic Equilibrium

Three identical small charged spheres, each with a charge of +2.0 μC and mass 5.0 g, are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle with sides of length 30 cm. The spheres are released simultaneously. a) Calculate the initial acceleration of each sphere. b) If one of the charges were negative instead of positive, how would this change the motion of the system?

Problem 3.10: Application Problem - Electrostatic Precipitator

An electrostatic precipitator is used to remove dust particles from exhaust gases in an industrial chimney. The precipitator applies a voltage difference of 50 kV across parallel plates separated by 15 cm. a) Calculate the electric field strength between the plates. b) If a smoke particle of mass 1.5 × 10⁻¹⁵ kg acquires a charge of +8.0 × 10⁻¹⁷ C, calculate the electric force on it. c) Calculate the acceleration of the particle due to this electric force. d) If the particle enters the precipitator with a horizontal velocity of 2.0 m/s perpendicular to the field, how far will it travel horizontally before hitting one of the plates? (Assume the effect of gravity is negligible compared to the electric force.) ======= Problem Set 3: Electrostatics
